## Why six is structurally different from four

The four-trade matrix has rank23 and five rational invariant directions. Our new small integer invariant separates the primitive18 endpoints; the previous scalar invariant does not. Adding six-slot trades raises the rank to27, leaving only the exact target-count direction over the rationals. The determinant then proves that no EXTRA finite-index charge obstruction survives either: the remaining modular obstruction is exactly the original paired group, with no missing higher quotient.

The nineteen-slot helper route demonstrates actual feasibility for the marked endpoints. The lattice theorem explains why the relevant additive barrier disappears at six; the helper supplies an admissible sequence through the binary region. These are complementary certificates, not interchangeable proofs.

Integer generation alone does not guarantee legal intermediate states. Already moves2 and3 generate Z, but cannot connect0 and1 inside the permitted state set{0,1}. In our setting a signed integer combination may temporarily demand a negative slot count, repeat a source choice, or require a resource whose actual current option is unavailable. The theorem therefore concerns integer charge relations; the recorded four-event route supplies feasibility only for its declared endpoints.

The next precise question is whether every fixed-margin/current binary fibre of this28-source supply is connected by its six-slot trades, or whether a feasible-region obstruction survives despite complete additive generation. No exhaustive all-fibre claim is made here, and no constant-six all-order tournament rule follows.
